title: Fomo Kernel Trade Evaluation
description: One row per `review.py consider` call (docs/decision-fomo-kernel-shape.md Layer 2): a user mid-decision asks what a hypothetical trade does to their book, away from any review session. The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/review.py's cmd_consider holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. Stored in <root>/trade_evaluations.jsonl, append-only. Every field is a frozen value computed at the time of the ask, never a pointer into mutable state -- the ledger keeps growing after this row is written, and a later reconciliation must see what the engine actually said then, not what it would say now (the frozen-subject design ratified in issue #446's specification comment). A resolution (`--resolve`) appends a new row carrying the same evaluation_id rather than rewriting this one; the fold picks whichever row for that id appears last in the file.

evaluation_id.description: Engine-assigned, content-addressed identity (eval-<hash of premise+basis+created+consequence+rule_collisions, plus context when one was supplied>), the same convention session.py uses for snapshot_id/adjustment_id/reconciliation_id. Asking the identical premise again the same day against an unchanged book converges on the same id rather than minting a new one; asking it with a different stated why_now does not, because that is a different question about the same trade (issue #479). See review.py's _evaluation_id for why the seed carries the frozen result rather than an enumerated list of the inputs that produced it.

created.description: The date this evaluation was asked (today, at CLI invocation time) -- distinct from premise.date, which is when the hypothetical trade itself would happen.

premise.description: The normalized hypothetical trade consequence.validate_premise() returned: ticker, side, qty, price, date, currency. notional, when the caller supplied it, is already consumed into qty by validation time and never appears here.

context.description: The user's own reason, why-now and evidence references at the moment of the ask (issue #479), when the caller supplied them through --decision-context. The shape is declared once, in decision-context.schema.json, and $ref-ed here rather than restated -- the same treatment `premise` gets above. Absent, never null, on a call that carried no context: this property's presence is exactly the condition review.py's _evaluation_id uses to decide whether the context enters the identity seed, so a row without the key and a seed without the key are the same fact read twice. Frozen like every other field here -- a --resolve appends a new row carrying this context unchanged, and nothing rewrites, translates or re-derives the user's words afterwards.

basis.description: Frozen evaluation footing. Ledger-backed current-book evaluations carry PortfolioBasis identity/disclosures so a later reader can see exactly what holdings fact answered; explicit CSV input remains the separate historical FIFO compatibility lane and declares itself unverified rather than impersonating a reconciled current book.

source.description: PortfolioBasis source for ledger-backed current-book evaluation; transactions denotes the separate explicit CSV/FIFO compatibility lane.

as_of.description: The date of the record's own latest row -- the last trade or snapshot anchor the reconstructed book actually reflects.

stale_days.description: created minus as_of, in days. Disclosed, never gated on -- issue #456 leaves the question of an interruption-worthy threshold explicitly unresolved; a large value means the answer is confidently computed on a record that may no longer match the real book, not that the answer was refused.

completeness.description: How the frozen current-book source was obtained: declared_complete when a recorded book row anchored it, unverified when the book came from transaction replay alone. Disclosed, never gated on -- #485 removed the completeness gates and #549 removed the completeness flag itself. declared_partial is retained for replay compatibility only: no engine path can produce it since #549, and a stored row carrying it predates that change.

cost_basis.description: Cost convention used by the frozen basis. fifo exists only for explicit CSV compatibility; canonical PortfolioBasis uses the other values.

valuation_basis.description: Whether the current-book basis carried a supplied valuation manifest. An unpriced consequence remains a disclosed cost-basis computation, not a zero-price valuation.

reconciliation_ref.description: The selected canonical snapshot anchor, if one exists.

state_version.description: Deterministic basis identity. PortfolioBasis uses pb-v1:<sha256>; CSV compatibility uses its own csv-v1:<sha256> identity and is not a current-book reconciliation version.

valuation_coverage.description: Canonical sizing projection coverage for a ledger-backed current-book evaluation. This makes mixed price/cost fallback visible; absent on the separate CSV compatibility lane.

consequence.description: The frozen return of engine/consequence.py's consequence(). before/after/delta are not restated field-by-field here -- that shape belongs to consequence.py alone, the same posture session-bundle.schema.json takes toward engine_state/engine_card.

before.description: portfolio_state() over the book alone. See consequence.py for the field contract.

after.description: portfolio_state() over the book plus the hypothetical trade. See consequence.py for the field contract.

delta.description: Signed after-minus-before changes for the readings that moved; a field absent here did not move. See consequence.py's _delta().

excluded_holdings.description: Held positions that could not be valued, and are therefore outside the denominator every number above is measured against (#515). Empty when the whole book was usable. The identities live here rather than inside `disclosures`, which is machine-readable keys and never carries data: `partial_book` says THAT something was excluded, this says WHAT. Any consumer stating a derived number must name these alongside it -- a partial denominator that does not say it is partial is worse than the refusal it replaced.

reason.description: Which fact was missing. Engine-assigned; never a user or agent claim.

disclosures.description: Machine-readable limitation keys, mirroring consequence.DISCLOSURES. Locale wording belongs in renderer copy, never here (CLAUDE.md, "Honesty decisions belong in code").

rule_collisions.description: One row per currently-tracked rule, mirroring engine/consequence.py's rule_collision(). A muted rule is excluded, matching the rotation it opted out of.

text.description: The rule's own text, verbatim, as stored on rules.jsonl.

problem_key.description: null means this rule's metric_key has no mechanical mapping at all -- state is unmapped, never a silent pass.

state.description: Mirrors consequence.COLLISION_STATES. would_breach: this trade is what freshly crosses the line. already_over: the book was already over the line and stays there, with or without this trade being the cause -- never read as this trade breaking the rule. unjudged: a metric this module cannot evaluate from one hypothetical trade (exit_severity, hold_severity). unmapped: problem_key is null.

worsens.description: Set only when state is already_over: whether this trade moves the relevant reading in the bad direction. null everywhere else -- a boolean that means nothing outside one state is worse than an absent one.

decision.description: What the user did with this evaluation. open until a --resolve call records one of the other three; never rewritten in place -- --resolve appends a new row with the same evaluation_id.

decided_on.description: The date --resolve recorded a decision (ISO date), or null while decision is open.

agent_case.description: Optional structured case for and against the trade, supplied by the caller through --agent-case and checked by engine/answer_provenance.py::validate_agent_case against this row's own frozen basis/consequence/rule_collisions before the row is ever written (#414, wired in by #479 Wave B). Never required, and never free prose -- owner ruling 2026-07-27: the agent lists the case for and against and does not take a position, so a submission missing either side is refused rather than accepted one-sided. The shape is declared once, in answer-provenance.schema.json, and $ref-ed here rather than restated -- the same treatment `premise` and `context` get above. That file's own description explains why the shape could not stay this schema's own additionalProperties:false claim $defs: which fields a claim may carry (`anchor`/`worsens`, or `source`/`as_of`) depends on its provenance, and reconciling the two was Wave B's integration decision.
